sections.title: Sound of letter S
paragraphs: The letter (S) /s/ has four sounds. Its main sound is a voiceless hiss. Voiceless means your voice is off and your throat does not shake. You hear this clear hiss in the word (sun) /sʌn/, which means the bright star in the daytime sky.

sections.title: How to say S
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push air through the small gap with no voice. For the second sound, make the same hiss but turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the third sound, pull your tongue slightly back and let your voice buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules for S
paragraphs: At the start of words, say the voiceless hiss, as in (sit) /sɪt/. After a voiceless consonant, say this same sound, as in (cats) /kæts/. Between vowels, turn your voice on, as in (rose) /roʊz/. After voiced sounds at word ends, keep your voice on, as in (dogs) /dɒɡz/. Before special endings like -ion after a vowel, make a buzzing sound, as in (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/. The letter is not pronounced in (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with S
paragraphs: Many learners forget to turn their voice on at the end of common words. Do not say a voiceless hiss at the end of (dogs) /dɒɡz/. Touch your throat and feel the vibration to make a clean buzz. Another mistake is pronouncing silent letters. Do not say any consonant sound for this letter when you say (island) /aɪ.lənd/.
